title: Script Shelf
description: Scripts for high-content imaging and everyday lab data chores: Fiji macros, PowerShell, Python and Excel VBA.

scripts.name: Composite Batch
scripts.summary: Batch-export flattened colour composites from single-channel high-content images, such as CX7 .C01 exports.
scripts.description: Lists the image files in a source folder (optionally with well subfolders) and assigns each file to a channel using a text per channel, for example a name containing "DAPI". Files in the same folder whose names are identical once the channel text is removed form one set, which becomes one composite. Each channel gets one colour and one fixed display range applied to every set, so intensities stay comparable. The ranges can be set automatically from randomly picked sets or tuned by eye on a preview. Each set is exported as a flattened RGB composite, with optional single-channel images, scale bar and burned-in label, and a run log is written next to the outputs.
requirements: Bio-Formats (bundled with Fiji) to open non-TIFF files such as Cellomics .C01
usage: In Fiji: Plugins > Macros > Run... and choose Composite_Batch.ijm. For a menu entry, copy the file to Fiji.app/plugins/ and restart Fiji.
Folders: choose the source folder (tick 'Include subfolders' for plate\well layouts), the destination folder, the file extensions (default .C01) and the number of channels.
Channel rules: type one text per channel (e.g. DAPI, GFP), then check the grouping summary: counts per channel, complete and incomplete sets, an example set.
Colours and ranges: one LUT and a fixed min/max per channel. 'Auto' derives them from N random sets (median or mean, default 20); 'Preview' opens a set to tune with Brightness/Contrast.
Export: format (PNG, TIFF, JPEG), name suffix, folder structure, overwrite, optional single-channel images, scale bar and label.
inputs: Single-channel images, one file per channel (.C01 by default, .tif/.tiff also), in one folder or in plate\well subfolders
Files of the same field share their name apart from the channel text
outputs: <name>_<channel>.<ext>: optional single-channel images in their colour
CompositeBatch_log_<date-time>.txt: file list, grouping, all settings, every file written or skipped
warnings: Not yet run in Fiji: written on 2026-11-05 without access to Fiji.
1 to 7 channels. Images of a set must have the same size and bit depth; other sets are skipped and logged.
Stacks: only the first plane is used.
JPEG quality follows Edit > Options > Input/Output.

scripts.name: Overlay Viewer
scripts.summary: Browse microscopy images with their segmentation outlines on top, with one display setting for all images.
scripts.description: You pick one image and its matching outline file as examples; the macro works out how the two file names differ, scans the plate folder including well subfolders, and pairs every image with its outline by name (well folder + name without the ending), so empty wells without a segmentation do not shift the pairing. A control window sets the display min/max and LUT once and applies them to every image while you browse; outlines are drawn in one colour with black transparent. All overlays can be exported as RGB PNG with the display settings burned in. The folder also holds Overlay_Viewer.ijm, a different variant of the same tool (see Warnings).

versions.label: Overlay_Viewer.ijm (other variant)
versions.note: Learns the naming pattern from a picked pair, reads Cellomics .C01 outline files with a built-in Jython reader, and adds outline opacity and thickness, histogram, PNG/TIFF/JPEG export and a vertical-flip option.

requirements: Overlay_Viewer.ijm variant: Bio-Formats and Fiji's Jython (both bundled with Fiji) for .C01 outlines
usage: Copy the macro, then in Fiji: Plugins > New > Macro, paste, then Run. To keep it, save it as Overlay_Viewer_v2.ijm in Fiji's macros folder.
Choose one microscopy image, then its matching outline file. The macro scans the plate folder.
Check what was detected (folder to scan, name endings of images and outlines), optionally tick 'Only show images that have an outline'.
In the control window, set display min/max, LUT and outline colour; OK applies them and re-opens the window. 'After OK' = Go to next steps through the images.
Tick 'Export all overlays as PNG' and choose a folder to save every overlay. Cancel quits; images stay open.
inputs: Plate folder with microscopy images and outline images (e.g. exported from HCS Studio), optionally in well subfolders
Outline images: black (0) = background, any other grey = outline; same width and height as the image
outputs: NNNN_<image name>_overlay.png: RGB overlays with the display settings burned in
warnings: 2D single-channel images: only the first plane of a stack is used.
An outline image of a different size is overlaid misaligned (a warning is logged).
Two variants are kept (Overlay_Viewer_v2.ijm and Overlay_Viewer.ijm); which one is current is not documented.

scripts.name: Group images by well
scripts.summary: Sort a flat CX7 / HCS Studio image export into one subfolder per well.
scripts.description: Reads the well ID from each file name, following the HCS Studio pattern <plate>_<well>f<field>d<channel> (e.g. ..._A04f00d1), and moves the file into a folder named after that well, created next to the images. Well IDs of one or two letters plus two digits are recognised, so 1536-well IDs such as AF48 work too. A summary at the end lists the files moved per well, in plate order.
usage: Preview first (moves nothing): .\Group-ImagesByWell.ps1 -Path "D:\Exports\Plate1" -WhatIf
Then run the same command without -WhatIf.
For files other than .tif/.tiff, pass the extensions, e.g. -Extensions .C01
If Windows blocks scripts: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Group-ImagesByWell.ps1 -Path "D:\Exports\Plate1"
inputs: -Path: folder containing the images (default: current folder)
outputs: One subfolder per well, with the matching files moved into it
Console summary: wells, files moved, skipped or failed, files not recognised, files per well
warnings: Moves files rather than copying them.
Only files directly inside -Path are processed; subfolders are ignored.
Never overwrites: a file already in its well folder is skipped.
Files without a recognisable well ID are left in place and listed.
Images from several plates in one folder are grouped into the same well folders; a warning names the plates.

scripts.name: Move exports to the network drive
scripts.summary: Move local exports to a network share: copy, check size and date, and only then delete the original.
scripts.description: Checks that the local export folder and the network destination are both reachable, and stops without touching anything otherwise. It takes the files not modified for N minutes (2 by default), copies each one to the network keeping the folder structure, compares size and modification date (2 s tolerance), and deletes the original only when both match; a failure keeps the original and is logged. First-level folders emptied by the transfer are moved into a "_" subfolder of the export folder, which is never scanned. A lock file prevents two runs at once and a log is written per month. Comments and messages are in French. Two double-click launchers come with it: a real run and a simulation.

versions.label: First version
versions.note: Deletes the emptied local subfolders instead of moving them into "_".

requirements: Write access to the network destination for the account that runs it
usage: Put Move-ExportToNetwork.ps1 and the two .bat launchers together in one folder outside the export folder, e.g. C:\Outils_Transfert.
Open the .ps1 in Notepad and set the 4 lines under 'A MODIFIER': $SourceDir, $DestDir (prefer a \\server\share UNC path to a drive letter), $MinAgeMinutes, $LogDir (outside $SourceDir).
Dry run: double-click Lancer_Simulation.bat (or run the script with -DryRun). It lists what would be moved and changes nothing.
Test on copies of a small export, then use Lancer_Transfert.bat for real transfers.
inputs: $MinAgeMinutes: files modified more recently are skipped
outputs: Files moved to the network with the same folder structure
warnings: Published version: 2026-11-05 with placeholder paths (\\SERVEUR\Partage). A later working version (progress display, archive folder next to the logs) is not published because it contains internal network paths.
A file with the same name already at the destination is overwritten.
-DryRun does not simulate the archiving into "_".
Not run here: written without access to Windows.

scripts.name: Move TIFFs into an images subfolder
scripts.summary: Create an "images" subfolder and move every .tif / .tiff of the folder into it.
scripts.description: Put the script in the folder that holds the TIFFs and run it. It creates an "images" subfolder there and moves every .tif / .tiff file of that folder into it. Subfolders are not searched. A file that already exists in images is skipped, never overwritten; a file still open in another program is reported and left in place. A summary shows how many files were moved, skipped or failed.
usage: Put the script in the folder with the TIFFs, then right-click it > Run with PowerShell.
Preview without moving anything: .\move_tiffs_to_images.ps1 -WhatIf
Another folder or subfolder name: .\move_tiffs_to_images.ps1 -Folder <folder> -Subfolder raw
If Windows blocks scripts: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\move_tiffs_to_images.ps1
inputs: -Folder: folder to process (default: the script's folder)
-Subfolder: name of the subfolder to create (default: images)
outputs: The subfolder, with the TIFFs moved into it
Console summary of moved, skipped and failed files
warnings: Moves files rather than copying them.
When started from the console host it waits for Enter before closing (last line of the script).

scripts.name: Fridge inventory basket (Panier)
scripts.summary: Double-click a tube's position in an Excel inventory to put it in the basket, take it out or put it back, with every action archived.
scripts.description: Version 2 of the fridge-inventory 'Panier' macros. Each box in a sheet named "Rack ..." has a "Panier" column; double-clicking a position number puts the tube in the basket (a tick), then either marks it as taken out (position emptied) or puts it back. The "Panier" sheet is a view of all tubes in the basket, rebuilt whenever it is opened, and double-clicking one of its rows jumps to the tube. Every action is written to an "Archive" sheet first (date, user, action, location, tube contents). EquiperRacks sets the orange highlighting of basket rows by conditional formatting. Boxes are found from their merged "Box ..." title and header row, so no column number is fixed in the code. Comments and messages are in French.
requirements: Inventory sheets named "Rack ..." with the box layout of the "Rack Modèle" sheet: merged "Box ..." title, header row ending with "Panier", one numbered position per row
usage: Work on a copy of the stock file saved as .xlsm.
VBA editor (Alt+F11) > Insert > Module, paste modPanier (the main module).
Insert > Module, paste modEquiperPanier.
Double-click ThisWorkbook in the VBA editor and paste the ThisWorkbook code; nothing else goes in ThisWorkbook.
Alt+F8 > EquiperRacks once to set the orange highlighting; run it again after copying a box inside a sheet (not needed after copying a whole sheet).
Double-click a position number (first column of a box) to use the basket.
inputs: Sheets named "Rack ..." laid out as "Rack Modèle"
outputs: "Panier" sheet: current basket, rebuilt on activation
Orange highlighting of tubes in the basket
warnings: The files are code to paste into the VBA editor: they have no export header, so File > Import is not the route.
Nothing happens when the workbook is open read-only (a message explains why).
